item.title: Atum Azul
item.description: Due to its economic importance in cuisine, especially in sushi and sashimi, bluefin tuna is the target of significant fishing, facing serious challenges due to overfishing and habitat degradation, and is classified as vulnerable by the IUCN.

item.title: Baleia-azul
item.description: The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) has listed blue whales as endangered.

item.title: Lula-comum
item.description: It is a species of squid that lives in the waters of the Mediterranean and the Atlantic.

item.title: Medusa
item.description: Some small fish are immune to jellyfish stings and live among the tentacles, serving as bait in a fish trap; they are safe from potential predators and can share the fish caught by the jellyfish. Jellyfish cause skin burns, which can sometimes lead to beaches being closed.

item.title: Pinguim-Imperador
item.description: Population declines of 50% in the Adélie Land region (French Antarctic) were observed due to increased adult mortality, especially among males, during an abnormally warm and prolonged period in the late 1970s, which resulted in decreased ice cover. On the other hand, the egg incubation success rate decreased when the ice shelf over the sea increased. The species is therefore considered to be very sensitive to climate change.

item.title: Polvo-comum
item.description: These animals have developed great intelligence due to survival needs, for example, due to the fragility of their bodies (lack of a shell).

item.title: Tartaruga-marinha
item.description: The group consists of six genera and seven species, all of which are threatened with extinction due to many years of intensive hunting for their shells.

item.title: Tubarão-branco
item.description: It is currently the largest predatory fish. The International Union for Conservation of Nature lists the great white shark as a vulnerable species, and it is included in the Endangered Species List, being protected by several governments.
